title: Investors Love Thematic ETFs and Mutual Funds, but They Aren’t Always Loved Back - WSJ
summary: This article discusses the popularity of thematic ETFs and mutual funds among investors, despite their potential for disappointment. It highlights how these funds allow investors to target specific industries like space, AI, or clean energy. The article also mentions the performance of several thematic funds through October, suggesting that investors should approach them with caution.

title: UPS expects a record-breaking 1.9 million returns on National Returns Day
summary: UPS forecasts a record 1.9 million returns on National Returns Day, marking a 26% increase from the previous year. This will be the seventh consecutive record broken on National Returns Day, driven by the ongoing growth of e-commerce activities. The article highlights how Amazon's convenient delivery and return services contribute to this trend.

title: State Street SPDR S&P Kensho Future Security ETF Trade Ideas — AMEX:FITE
summary: This article discusses investment opportunities in military technology and state security, driven by a rise in populism and the increasing involvement of disruptive tech companies. It highlights how major tech firms like Amazon and Microsoft are engaging with defense contracts and notes the significant returns seen in the defense and aerospace sector, outperforming other market segments. The piece suggests that this trend signifies a long-term shift towards greater spending on advanced security technologies.

title: Fiserv and ExxonMobil will Enable Consumers to Fill Up by Asking Alexa to Pay at the Pump
summary: Fiserv and ExxonMobil announced a partnership to allow consumers to pay for fuel at over 11,500 Exxon and Mobil stations using Amazon Alexa. This new voice-activated payment method, powered by Fiserv's digital commerce technology and Amazon Pay, will be available later in 2020 and demonstrated at CES 2020. It aims to provide a frictionless and secure transaction experience for consumers in Alexa-enabled vehicles or using other Alexa mobility devices.

title: FedEx Begins Construction on Distribution Facility in Florida
summary: FedEx has started construction on a new 42,000-square-foot distribution center near the Gainesville, Florida airport, a project expected to cost around $9 million and add 20 jobs. This new facility will replace a currently leased FedEx location and is strategically located to cater to the growing online commerce in the area. Other major logistics players like Amazon and UPS are also expanding or considering expansion in Gainesville and Ocala, highlighting the region's importance for distribution.

title: 19 Top Identity Management Solutions
summary: This article identifies 19 top identity management solutions, explaining their role in modern cybersecurity, particularly within a "zero trust" framework. It details the features and benefits of each solution, highlighting how they enhance security by managing user access and credentials. The solutions discussed range from multi-factor authentication tools to comprehensive IT-HR platforms designed to streamline access control and improve data protection.

title: MTBC Acquires Cloud-based EHR Platform CareCloud - Healthcare M&A
summary: MTBC, a provider of cloud-based healthcare IT and revenue cycle management solutions, announced the acquisition of CareCloud, a cloud-based practice management EHR platform. This acquisition aims to accelerate MTBC's strategic roadmap by integrating CareCloud's advanced technology and expanding its network of healthcare providers. The deal was completed on a cash-free, debt-free basis and is expected to drive growth and operational efficiencies for the combined entities.

title: New FIS headquarters in Brooklyn wins conceptual design approval
summary: The proposed Fidelity National Information Services Inc. (FIS) world headquarters in Brooklyn received unanimous conceptual design approval. The 12-story, 350,000 square-foot office tower will include an eight-story parking garage with mixed-use office and retail space, though its public accessibility was a point of discussion. The project, valued at $145 million, aims to consolidate FIS's Jacksonville operations and create 500 new jobs by 2022.

title: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos to Face Protests From ‘Enraged’ Local Merchants During India Visit
summary: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos is expected to encounter significant protests from local merchants during his visit to India. These merchants, organized under the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT), plan sit-ins and rallies across 300 cities to protest Amazon's pricing and exclusive selling practices, which they argue harm small businesses. The protests coincide with Bezos's participation in Amazon India’s "smbhav" event, highlighting growing resentment against the company's business model in a critical market.

title: Amazon lifts ban on FedEx Ground for third-party Prime shipments
summary: Amazon has lifted its ban on FedEx Ground for third-party Prime shipments, nearly a month after imposing it. The decision comes after Amazon notified its third-party merchants that they could once again use FedEx's service. This change follows Amazon's assessment that FedEx's service levels have improved since the Christmas rush.

title: Amazon lifts ban on FedEx Ground for third-party Prime shipments
summary: Amazon has lifted its ban on FedEx Ground for third-party Prime shipments, nearly a month after imposing it. The decision comes after Amazon noted improved FedEx service levels, while FedEx stated its network performed well during the peak season. This reversal allows third-party merchants to once again use FedEx's Ground network for Amazon Prime orders.

title: Target was strong where it needed strength, and that bodes well for the rest of the year
summary: Target's 2019 holiday sales missed expectations, causing a stock selloff, primarily due to weakness in electronics, toys, and home goods. Despite the overall miss, the company showed strength in key investment areas like apparel, beauty, and food, which analysts believe bodes well for its long-term strategy and profitability. CEO Brian Cornell expressed confidence, maintaining the retailer's earnings outlook due to strong gross margin mix and effective digital fulfillment.

title: Can Baby Yoda save Build-A-Bear?
summary: Build-A-Bear, once a successful toy company that went public in 2004, has seen its financial fortunes decline significantly due to struggles in brick-and-mortar retail. The company's stock, which once hit $36.90, averaged $4.37 over the last year, leading to predictions of zero growth or a small drop for the fiscal year 2019. However, the announcement of a Baby Yoda plush toy, a collaboration with Disney's popular "The Mandalorian" series, caused Build-A-Bear's stock to skyrocket 15%, offering a potential lifeline for the struggling retailer.

title: San Jose city, business leaders announce new ‘Innovation Zone’
summary: San Jose city officials and business leaders have announced a new "innovation zone" on the city's west side, encompassing parts of District 1 and District 6. This zone will allow companies like Bird, Siemens, Amazon Web Services, and Verizon to test new technologies, with early pilots including "anti-sidewalk" technology for scooters. Additionally, discussions are underway to convert the historic Century 21 theater building into an "Innovation Hub."

title: Moderna Partners with AWS to Explore the ‘Software of Life’
summary: Moderna is partnering with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to accelerate the development of personalized therapies, particularly for cancer, by leveraging AWS's cloud computing platforms for gene sequencing. Moderna's CEO, Stephane Bancel, likens messenger RNA (mRNA) to "software of life" and highlights its potential in directing the body to produce therapeutic proteins. The collaboration aims to speed up the drug development process from preclinical to clinical phases and is already being used for over a dozen drug candidates.

title: Up Over 110%, the ONLN ETF Is the Only Thing on Many a Christmas List
summary: The ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN) has surged nearly 113% year-to-date, driven by the acceleration of e-commerce due to the pandemic. Analysts predict a significant increase in online holiday sales, with Adobe Analytics forecasting a 33% year-over-year surge to $189 billion. Despite this growth, online retail still represents a relatively small portion of total retail sales, indicating substantial future growth potential.

title: Austin-based Wikibuy is Booming Since its Acquisition by Capital One
summary: Austin-based Wikibuy has experienced significant growth and success since its acquisition by Capital One in November 2018. The company has expanded its employee base and user count, evolving from a comparison-shopping engine to include features like automatic coupon application and cash-back rebates. Wikibuy continues to operate from Austin, contributing to the city's booming e-commerce sector.

title: Intel Board of Directors Elects New Chairman and New Director
summary: Intel Corporation announced that Andy D. Bryant stepped down as chairman of the board, and Dr. Omar Ishrak was elected to succeed him as independent chairman, effective immediately. Additionally, Alyssa Henry was elected to Intel’s board, marking the seventh new independent director added since 2016. Bryant will remain on the board until the 2020 annual stockholders’ meeting to facilitate a smooth transition.

title: Tesla created demand for electric cars, but only for Teslas
summary: Despite a surge in new electric vehicle models hitting the market, Tesla remains the dominant player and virtually the only car company profiting from EV sales. Traditional automakers are hesitant to fully embrace EVs due to high costs, range anxiety among consumers, and the expectation that supply will outpace demand. While government mandates are driving EV adoption in other regions, the US market is slower to shift, with hybrids still preferred by many consumers over pure electrics.

title: Top 16 best datacenter service providers in India
summary: This article lists the top 16 data center service providers in India, highlighting the booming demand for data center infrastructure driven by increasing internet users and cloud adoption. It details each company's offerings, locations, and key features to assist businesses in choosing a suitable provider. The list includes both global and local players, detailing their services and infrastructure.

title: The five biggest tech companies now make up 17.5% of the S&P 500 — here's how to protect yourself
summary: The five largest tech companies (Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Facebook) now comprise 17.5% of the S&P 500, leading to potential overexposure for passive investors. Financial advisors are suggesting strategies like equal-weighted funds, specialized tech ETFs focusing on emerging areas, and ESG investments to diversify portfolios. While Big Tech's dominance has driven strong returns, advisors emphasize balancing diversification with access to growth, cautioning against timing the market with large active bets.

title: Which tech stock is best? Here’s how the ‘big five’ companies stack up as they report earnings
summary: This article examines how the "big five" U.S. tech companies are positioned as they prepare to report their quarterly earnings. It highlights Amazon as the favorite among analysts, while Apple is deemed the "cheapest" despite its recent stock performance. The article sets out to compare some of their key numbers ahead of Apple kicking off the earnings season.

title: Which tech stock is best? Here’s how the ‘big five’ companies stack up as they report earnings
summary: MarketWatch discusses how the "big five" U.S. tech companies compare as they prepare to report earnings. Amazon is noted as an analyst favorite, while Apple is deemed the "cheapest" despite its recent stock run-up. The article previews the upcoming earnings reports, with Apple kicking off the round.

title: IBM's Ginni Rometty stepping down as CEO for cloud computing chief
summary: Ginni Rometty is stepping down as CEO of IBM, with Arvind Krishna, the current senior vice president for cloud and cognitive software, set to take over on April 6. Rometty will remain executive chairman until the end of the year. James Whitehurst, CEO of Red Hat, will become president of IBM.

title: FedEx Has a Plan to Battle Amazon Shipping, CEO Says
summary: FedEx CEO Fred Smith outlines his strategy for battling Amazon in the shipping industry and overcoming recent setbacks. He plans to position FedEx as an anti-Amazon ally for retailers, aiming to surpass UPS in size and become the most cost-efficient ground courier. Smith expresses confidence his plan will prove successful despite past challenges and current skepticism from analysts.

title: IBM CEO Ginni Rometty stepping down, cloud boss Arvind Krishna to succeed
summary: Ginni Rometty is stepping down as CEO of IBM after eight years, with cloud boss Arvind Krishna set to succeed her in April. Rometty, a 40-year IBM veteran, spearheaded numerous acquisitions, including the $34 billion Red Hat deal, as the company worked to catch up in the cloud services market. Despite a recent revenue growth, IBM's stock value declined about a quarter during her tenure, and the company's turnaround remains ongoing.

title: Go behind the scenes as Amazon develops a new electric vehicle
summary: Amazon and Rivian are collaborating to introduce thousands of custom electric delivery vans to 100 U.S. cities by the end of the year, aiming to build the world's most sustainable transportation fleet. This initiative is part of Amazon's commitment to The Climate Pledge, an effort to become net zero carbon by 2040 and reduce millions of metric tons of carbon annually by 2030. The new vehicles emphasize driver safety, optimize technology and design, and integrate Amazon's logistics management and Alexa for a seamless delivery experience.

title: IITian Arvind Krishna to be new IBM CEO, replacing Ginni Rometty
summary: International Business Machines Corp. has named Arvind Krishna as its new chief executive officer, succeeding Ginni Rometty. Krishna, previously head of IBM’s cloud and cognitive software unit, was a key architect of the Red Hat acquisition and will take over after Rometty retires later this year. The announcement was well-received by the market, with shares rising 5% in extended trading, as analysts view the leadership change as a positive and overdue step for the company's innovation in hybrid cloud.

title: IIT Kanpur graduate Arvind Krishna is new IBM CEO
summary: Arvind Krishna, an IIT Kanpur graduate and head of IBM’s cloud business, will take over as CEO from Ginni Rometty in April. Rometty, who led the company for eight years and oversaw the $34 billion Red Hat acquisition, will continue as executive chairman until the end of the year. The transition comes as IBM continues its efforts to rejuvenate and boost its cloud services business.

title: Arvind Krishna, the man who helped buy Red Hat, now wears the CEO hat at IBM
summary: Arvind Krishna has been named the new CEO of IBM, replacing Virginia Rometty. Krishna, known for being the principal architect behind IBM’s $34 billion acquisition of Red Hat, will lead the company as Rometty retires after nearly 40 years. This leadership change is seen as a welcome move to accelerate IBM's focus on hybrid cloud and AI after years of declining sales under Rometty.

title: Arvind Krishna named IBM CEO as company fights for cloud business spot
summary: IBM has named Arvind Krishna as its new CEO, taking over from Ginni Rometty, as the company intensifies its efforts to compete in the cloud services market. IBM was a late entrant to this sector, which is currently dominated by Amazon and Microsoft. Rometty's tenure was marked by 65 acquisitions, including the significant $34 billion Red Hat deal, aimed at boosting IBM's cloud presence.

title: Sierra-Cedar to Sell Workday, Salesforce, and U.S. MuleSoft Practices to Accenture
summary: Sierra-Cedar announced an agreement to sell its Workday, Salesforce, and U.S. MuleSoft practices to Accenture, with approximately 275 professionals joining Accenture. The transaction allows Sierra-Cedar to enhance its focus and investment in core growth areas like Oracle Cloud and AWS, while its Indian MuleSoft practice remains unaffected. Sierra-Cedar will continue to operate as a dedicated technology partner to Oracle and AWS, led by CEO Cal Yonker.

title: IBM replaces CEO: Ginni Rometty is on her way out
summary: IBM has named Arvind Krishna as its new chief executive officer, replacing Ginni Rometty, who will transition to executive chairman before retiring at the end of the year. Krishna, a key architect of the Red Hat acquisition, will lead IBM's focus on hybrid cloud and AI. Rometty, the company's first female CEO, staked IBM's future on hybrid cloud and oversaw the $34 billion Red Hat purchase, though the company's market value and revenue declined during her tenure.
